note: FLT3-ITD cell lines (MV4-11, MOLM-13) and their mouse xenografts carried quizartinib and gilteritinib into patients; the ex-vivo plasma inhibitory assay on those cells became the human engagement read-out.
label: AML (FLT3)

engagement.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
engagement.note: Quizartinib (AC220) inhibited FLT3 at low nanomolar potency in FLT3-ITD cells and was active in mice at 1 mg/kg.
engagement.short: Quizartinib blocks FLT3 in cells and mice
engagement.quote: AC220 exhibits low nanomolar potency in biochemical and cellular assays and exceptional kinase selectivity, and in animal models is efficacious at doses as low as 1 mg/kg given orally once daily.

engagement.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
engagement.note: Plasma from quizartinib-dosed patients completely inhibited FLT3-ITD phosphorylation in the same cells, the readout the model used.
engagement.quote: FLT3-ITD phosphorylation was completely inhibited in an in vitro plasma inhibitory assay.
engagement.reason: Patient plasma inhibited FLT3 as predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Cortes 2013 cites the preclinical models but does not set them beside the patient data. Gilteritinib agreed later (>=90% inhibition at >=80 mg/day, Perl 2017 doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30416-3; NCT02014558 results posted 2019-02-20), no status change. Phase 1 enrolled irrespective of FLT3 status; the PIA reads the drug in patient plasma on FLT3-ITD cells, so it does not depend on patient genotype.
engagement.magnitude_basis: phospho-FLT3 inhibition, cells/xenograft vs patient-plasma PIA
engagement.population: Relapsed/refractory AML, FLT3-ITD and FLT3 wild-type (phase 1, not selected for FLT3)

dose.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
dose.note: Nanomolar cell potency and a 1 mg/kg effective mouse dose set the exposure target for quizartinib; no patient exposure yet.
dose.short: Cell potency sets the exposure target
dose.quote: AC220 exhibits low nanomolar potency in biochemical and cellular assays and exceptional kinase selectivity, and in animal models is efficacious at doses as low as 1 mg/kg given orally once daily.

dose.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
dose.note: Complete FLT3-ITD inhibition was reached at doses below the 200 mg/day MTD, and FLT3-ITD patients responded (9/17).
dose.quote: FLT3-ITD phosphorylation was completely inhibited in an in vitro plasma inhibitory assay.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract does not give the dose-by-dose PIA results.
dose.reason: Target exposure reached and drug worked
dose.judgement: Called same: the cell-derived target was reached below the MTD (DLT grade 3 QT at higher doses) and the drug later worked (QuANTUM-R). margin_stated false because the 2009 model papers' abstracts state no tolerated margin. Sato 2011 (doi:10.1182/blood-2010-01-266742) showed patient-level FLT3 ligand blunts quizartinib in vitro; FDA's 2023 Vanflyta review cites it for why higher marrow exposure may be needed, but registered doses did reach target. Gilteritinib agreed: >=90% inhibition at >=80 mg, MTD 300 mg (Perl 2017), 'no overt toxicity' in mice (Mori 2017 doi:10.1007/s10637-017-0470-z).
dose.population: Relapsed/refractory AML, FLT3-ITD and FLT3 wild-type (phase 1, not selected for FLT3)

efficacy.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
efficacy.note: Quizartinib was efficacious in FLT3-ITD mouse models at 1 mg/kg; no patient efficacy comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: AC220 exhibits low nanomolar potency in biochemical and cellular assays and exceptional kinase selectivity, and in animal models is efficacious at doses as low as 1 mg/kg given orally once daily.

efficacy.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase 2, no success bar set in advance, co-primary CRc and CR: CRc 46-56% in FLT3-ITD, CR only 3-4%; authors call quizartinib highly active. Scored under the single-arm and co-primary rulings.
efficacy.short: Quizartinib phase 2: CRc in half of FLT3-ITD
efficacy.quote: In cohort 2, 62 (46%) of 136 FLT3-ITD-positive patients achieved composite complete remission with five (4%) achieving complete remission
efficacy.judgement: Single-arm and co-primary designs are now scored. The model predicted a response; the authors call single-agent quizartinib highly active (CRc met, CR low), so same with source_calls_it partial. Earlier FLT3 inhibitors (midostaurin, lestaurtinib) had given only transient blast reductions before 2009, so the 2009 xenograft result is not treated as a retrodiction. QuANTUM-R (2019, OS) moved to patient_trials; ADMIRAL is gilteritinib and moved to its own track.

patient_trials.quote: Overall survival was longer for quizartinib than for chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0·76 [95% CI 0·58-0·98; p=0·02]).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour regression in mice vs composite complete remission in patients

efficacy.model: FLT3-ITD cell lines and MV4-11 xenografts
efficacy.note: Gilteritinib plus azacitidine shrank MV4-11 xenografts more than either alone (Ueno 2019); LACEWING, a combination trial vs azacitidine, stopped for OS futility. Year from Astellas press release 2020-12-21.
efficacy.quote: Median OS was 9.82 (GIL + AZA) and 8.87 (AZA) months (hazard ratio, 0.916; 95% CI, 0.529-1.585; P = .753). The study was closed based on the protocol-specified boundary for futility.
efficacy.reason: Xenograft combo benefit failed in LACEWING
efficacy.judgement: Called contra, not untested: Ueno 2019 (doi:10.18632/oncotarget.26811) reported that gilteritinib plus azacitidine shrank MV4-11 xenografts more than either alone, and said this supports trials in patients unfit for intensive chemotherapy, published before LACEWING read out. LACEWING missed its primary endpoint, OS. Points against: CRc did rise (58.1% vs 26.5%), which fits a tumour-volume readout, and 44.9% of the azacitidine arm later got therapy including FLT3 inhibitors. The primary endpoint governs, and one drug's contra outweighs another's same. Later positive trials (QuANTUM-First, quizartinib plus chemotherapy, 2023) do not lift it. Combination ruling: a member drug with an active partner is scored on the primary endpoint like any trial, on the gilteritinib track. Year 2020: Astellas announced the OS futility on 2020-12-21 (tier 5, earliest public date); Wang 2022 (tier 1) sets the status. The gilteritinib monotherapy result on this model (ADMIRAL, FDA-adjudicated CR/CRh 21.0% in 2018, OS in patient_trials) would be a retro entry, since the gilteritinib xenograft data were first public (Mori 2017) after quizartinib's patient responses; it and a 2013 opener are not appended because an earlier-dated entry after this 2020 one breaks the track's year order without reordering the cell.

patient_trials.quote: The median overall survival in the gilteritinib group was significantly longer than that in the chemotherapy group (9.3 months vs. 5.6 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49 to 0.83; P<0.001).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: combination over azacitidine alone: xenograft tumour volume vs patient overall survival

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 FLT3-ITD saturation mutagenesis resistance screen (in vitro)
efficacy.note: In vitro mutagenesis of FLT3-ITD in Ba/F3 cells named the kinase-domain residues whose mutation would make quizartinib stop working.
efficacy.quote: Here we report point mutations at three residues within the kinase domain of FLT3-ITD that confer substantial in vitro resistance to AC220 (quizartinib), an active investigational inhibitor of FLT3, KIT, PDGFRA, PDGFRB and RET
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. model_kind is ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro cell-line value; the system is an engineered murine cell line, not patient cells.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the screen's first use; the comparison appears in the same paper.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 FLT3-ITD saturation mutagenesis resistance screen (in vitro)
efficacy.note: Every one of eight patients who relapsed on quizartinib carried new FLT3 kinase-domain mutations at residues the screen had flagged (D835, F691). Gilteritinib relapses (McMahon 2019) kept as context: no saturation screen was run for gilteritinib. Crenolanib split to its own track.
efficacy.quote: evolution of AC220-resistant substitutions at two of these amino acid positions was observed in eight of eight FLT3-ITD-positive AML patients with acquired resistance to AC220.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The trial the eight patients came from (AC220 phase 1 NCT00462761 or phase 2 NCT00989261, whose results were first posted 2019-11-29) is not named in the abstract, so registry_date is left null. Whether the screen was run before the patient samples were sequenced is not stated.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction: which genotype loses response. Scored same, not retro: the resistance residues were unknown clinically before this paper, and the screen and patient sequencing are reported together. Two of three predicted residues appeared in patients (Y842 did not), so magnitude is direction_only.
efficacy.reason: Predicted resistance residues found in patients
efficacy.magnitude_basis: in vitro resistance residues vs residues mutated at relapse in patients

patient_trials.quote: Less frequently, secondary FLT3-F691L gatekeeper mutations or BCR-ABL1 fusions were identified at progression.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells expressing FLT3-D835Y (TKD) treated with gilteritinib (in vitro)
efficacy.population: relapsed/refractory AML with FLT3-TKD (D835/I836) mutation, gilteritinib
efficacy.note: Gilteritinib blocked Ba/F3 FLT3-D835Y growth, the basis for treating TKD patients; no TKD-only patient reached CR/CRh (0/18 pooled), which FDA judged too small to call.
efficacy.short: TKD 0/18 CR/CRh; FDA calls it inconclusive
efficacy.quote: The lack of any response in black patients (0/12) or in patients with a TKD mutation (0/18) does not necessarily indicate a lack of efficacy, since the numbers of patients in these groups are small.
efficacy.confidence_note: FDA pooled interim analysis of Studies 0101 and 0301 (ADMIRAL NCT02421939); PMR asked for >=30 TKD patients. ADMIRAL's final TKD subgroup (Perl 2019 NEJM) was not checked here and could settle the track. model_first_use_year is a proxy (review date); the sponsor's Ba/F3 work (Mori 2017) predates it.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first (proxy) use, which is also the first patient comparison. Model readout: the same review states gilteritinib 'decreased proliferation' of FLT3-D835Y Ba/F3 cells. The regulator called the patient result inconclusive (upper 95% bound 19%), so the status is untested, not contra.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 FLT3-ITD saturation mutagenesis resistance screen (in vitro)
efficacy.note: The same Ba/F3 FLT3-ITD screen run with crenolanib recovered no resistant clones, predicting no kinase-domain resistance in patients.
efficacy.short: Screen predicts no crenolanib KD resistance
efficacy.quote: A saturation mutagenesis screen of FLT3-internal tandem duplication failed to recover any resistant colonies in the presence of a crenolanib concentration well below what has been safely achieved in humans
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry of the crenolanib track on this screen.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 FLT3-ITD saturation mutagenesis resistance screen (in vitro)
efficacy.note: Sequencing before and after crenolanib found no new FLT3 kinase-domain mutations and rare gatekeeper mutations; resistance came through NRAS, IDH2 and other genes, as the screen predicted.
efficacy.short: No FLT3 KD mutations at crenolanib relapse
efficacy.quote: Unlike other FLT3 inhibitors, crenolanib does not induce FLT3 secondary mutations, and mutations of the FLT3 gatekeeper residue are infrequent.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Earlier congress abstracts of these data not searched.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me with Smith 2014. Split from the quizartinib entry because crenolanib patients differ in result (no FLT3 secondary mutations). Not a retrodiction: crenolanib relapse genotypes were unknown in 2014.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: in vitro resistant colonies vs FLT3 mutations acquired at relapse
efficacy.population: FLT3-mutated relapsed/refractory AML treated with crenolanib
efficacy.reason: Crenolanib relapses lack predicted KD mutations

patient_trials.quote: Unlike other FLT3 inhibitors, crenolanib does not induce FLT3 secondary mutations, and mutations of the FLT3 gatekeeper residue are infrequent.

safety.model: Rat and dog toxicology and safety pharmacology
safety.note: Gilteritinib showed no CNS effects in rats, no cardiovascular effects in dogs and weak hERG block before first-in-human dosing.
safety.short: Tox species: no CNS or heart signal
safety.quote: There were no toxicologically significant effects at doses of gilteritinib up to 100 mg/kg in the central nervous system (CNS) of rats or in the cardiovascular or respiratory systems of dogs.
safety.confidence_note: Opened at 2013, the first-in-human year (NCT02014558), as a proxy for when the GLP package existed; it was made public only in the 2018 review.

safety.model: Rat and dog toxicology and safety pharmacology
safety.note: Patients on gilteritinib developed PRES with seizures and QT prolongation, which the rat CNS and dog cardiovascular studies had not shown.
safety.short: PRES and QT missed by tox species
safety.quote: There have been rare reports of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) with symptoms including seizure and altered mental status with XOSPATA.
safety.confidence_note: Label and review read in full text; the review does not itself set the null rat CNS study beside PRES.
safety.judgement: Scored the silence: rats can show seizures and the Irwin screen to 100 mg/kg was clean; dogs and hERG were clean, yet the label warns of QTcF >500 ms (1.7% in the review). Differentiation syndrome is not scored: healthy toxicology animals have no leukaemic blasts to differentiate, like a mouse and CRS. Quizartinib's monkey telemetry did predict its dose-limiting QT prolongation (FDA Vanflyta review 2023, Cortes 2013), but that comparison was public only in 2023 and a failed cell is not lifted by another drug's match.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence of CNS and QT harm
